questions.stem: Why must the shoot be cut underwater when setting up a potometer?

options.text: To keep the leaves wet so they can photosynthesise
To prevent air bubbles entering the xylem, which would break the water column
To wash off any soil from the roots
To allow the shoot to absorb water through the cut surface

questions.explanation: If the shoot is cut in air, air bubbles can enter the xylem vessels and break the continuous water column. This would prevent water from being pulled up by transpiration and give inaccurate results.
